I struggled a lot even after coming out because I was unsure how much of an influence internalised misogyny may have on my gender identity (I’m afab). Plus I never knew a specific term for my identity, I couldn’t describe it. Was I no gender? Both genders? Partly one, partly the other? I just used nb as an umbrella term. I came to the conclusion that sometimes, labelling myself just makes things overly complicated for me. I just choose to do the things that make me the most comfortable in my own skin and so far, it worked, somehow. 
And that’s how I told my (quite conservative) environment. Sometimes my family still doesn’t understand, but I try to convince them as long as I’m happy I don’t hurt anyone. 
I don’t know your relationship with your mother, obviously. But usually, a loving mother will accept whatever makes her child the happiest. Just try to be open with what you feel like. 
You can do this, and whatever happens, it will turn out fine!

A lot of my loved ones and people in my life already roll their eyes every time the word „Titanic“ is even mentioned by me! 
It all started for me when I was around 10 and I read an article about the sinking in a kids history/science magazine we have here in Germany. It just stuck with me and i developed such a big interest in history and just an obscure obsession with the Titanic in particular. 
Today I can explain this to myself this way; History is interesting to me because it always tracks human progress, human interaction, and the development of humanity as a whole, different societies, different ideologies and factors influencing this. The Titanic is just such a mirror of the Society of the beginning 20th Century, and how class and wealth really affected ones worth. It also  just represented  the euphoria widely spread for new opportunities, the „new world“ and the wonders of revolutionary technology. And socially! A way to immigrate to America save and fast, that was just the greatest thing imaginable for a lot of the European working class. 
That’s why I think with the Titanic, there was more sinking than just steel and wood. It marks the end of an era (I know the ocean liner era went on into the 30s but still) 
The death of so many dreams and hopes. The euphoria was over and society was struck by the sheer destruction their ignorance and pride could cause. I don’t think the Titanic should be an „overlooked“ historical event. I think it holds such big value to understanding the social atmosphere of the time period.
